A_target.statement:
Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$ with $m \perp n$.
Then:
:$\Z / m n \Z \cong \Z / m \Z \times \Z / n \Z$

B_source.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring with unity]].
Let $I, J$ be [[Definition:Ideal of Ring|ideals]] of $R$ with $I + J = R$.
Then:
:$R / \paren {I \cap J} \cong R / I \times R / J$

validity_conditions: In Z, (m)+(n) = Z iff gcd(m,n)=1 (Bezout), so the ideals are comaximal.
The general ring CRT then specializes to Z/mnZ ~= Z/mZ x Z/nZ.
proof_plan:
By [[Bézout's Identity]], $m x + n y = 1$ for some $x, y \in \Z$, so $\ideal m + \ideal n = \Z$.
As $m \perp n$, $\ideal m \cap \ideal n = \ideal {\lcm \set {m, n} } = \ideal {m n}$.

By the [[Chinese Remainder Theorem (Commutative Algebra)|Chinese Remainder Theorem for rings]]:
:$\Z / \paren {\ideal m \cap \ideal n} \cong \Z / \ideal m \times \Z / \ideal n$
